On this day in 1987, as Filipinos journeyed home, the once-called “the unsinkable ship” MV Doña Paz collided with an oil tanker near the Tablas Strait, erupting in flames and sinking. This tragedy claimed over 4,000 lives and earned the grim title of “𝗔𝘀𝗶𝗮’𝘀 𝗧𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗰,” 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿.

On December 20, 1987, the ferry MV Doña Paz departed Tacloban for Manila but collided with the oil tanker MT Vector at 10:30 PM near the Tablas Strait. Carrying over 1,000 tons of fuel, the tanker ignited on impact, triggering a massive fire. With lights out, life vests locked, and no crew guidance, passengers faced a deadly choice: stay aboard or jump into burning waters. 

Both vessels sank within hours. Of an estimated 4,386 people, many of whom were unregistered, only 26 survived. Investigations later revealed severe safety lapses, overloading, and crew negligence. #Christmas #maritime #disaster
